title: Andrew W. Lo, MIT 15.401 Finance Theory I — Lectures 15–17: The CAPM and APT (Fall 2008)
use: Primary teaching reference for covariance risk, CAPM required returns, market-proxy estimation and the distinction between model implications and empirical evidence. Scope: slides 3–9,17–27; no historical example or empirical estimate is imported into the fictional lab.
verification: Opened actual 29-page PDF and read the relevant slide text and course attribution. Mathematical explanation and examples in the chapter are original; no claim that the whole source or all historical evidence was independently verified.

title: William F. Sharpe — Capital Asset Prices: A Theory of Market Equilibrium under Conditions of Risk (1964)
use: Original equilibrium argument connecting portfolio choice, common expectations, equal borrowing/lending terms and systematic covariance risk. The chapter supplies its own explicit SPD quadratic-objective proof and original clearing economy.
verification: Actual publisher full-text HTML inspected: Section II investor preferences and pure-interest-rate discussion, Section III equilibrium/common-belief assumptions and price adjustment, and Section IV systematic versus total risk. Published Journal of Finance 19(3), 425–442, September 1964. No source example or figure copied; the text's uncorrelated-versus-independent wording and broader economic-activity interpretation are not adopted. Not a current empirical validation or general existence theorem.

title: Eugene F. Fama and Kenneth R. French — The Capital Asset Pricing Model: Theory and Evidence (2004)
use: Primary author paper on the market portfolio/proxy problem, regression pricing restrictions, hypothesis interpretation and implementation limits. The chapter treats the paper's empirical assessment as dated 2004, not current market evidence.
verification: Actual 22-page Dartmouth-hosted PDF inspected: printed pp.25–26 scope/common beliefs; pp.29–34 risk-free assumptions, beta and zero-intercept tests, imprecise estimated betas and proxy-efficiency interpretation; pp.40–42 market-proxy, nontraded-wealth and rationality/model ambiguity. Publication Journal of Economic Perspectives 18(3), 25–46. No historical dataset, source portfolio, result magnitude or figure reproduced. Original counterexamples and pedagogical sample are independently constructed.
